# 05 Drive step-by-step fade reveal through an animation controller

## Outcome

`createAnimationController(svg, timeline)` reads the elements already tagged `siren-pending` in a
rendered SVG and exposes `{ totalSteps, currentStep, next(), reset() }`: `next()` reveals exactly
one step's worth of elements at a time (removing `siren-pending`, adding `siren-enter-fade`);
`reset()` returns to the initial hidden state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a hand-built SVG fixture matching the frozen conventions (node `A`: no `siren-pending`;
  node `B`: `siren-pending`, `data-siren-id="B"`; node `C`: `siren-pending`, `data-siren-id="C"`)
  and a `ResolvedTimeline` of `{1: ['B'], 2: ['C']}`, `createAnimationController` returns a
  controller with `totalSteps === 2` and `currentStep === 0`.
- [ ] Calling `next()` once removes `siren-pending` and adds `siren-enter-fade` on node `B` only
  (node `C` untouched), and sets `currentStep` to `1`.
- [ ] Calling `next()` a second time does the same for node `C`, and sets `currentStep` to `2`.
- [ ] Calling `next()` a third time (past the last step) is a no-op: no class changes, `currentStep`
  stays `2`, no error thrown.
- [ ] Calling `reset()` after two `next()` calls restores `siren-pending` (and removes
  `siren-enter-fade`) on both `B` and `C`, leaves `A` untouched (it never had `siren-pending`), and
  sets `currentStep` back to `0`.

## Test seam

`createAnimationController(svg: SVGSVGElement, timeline: ResolvedTimeline): AnimationController`
— component test under Vitest's jsdom environment, hand-built SVG + `ResolvedTimeline` fixtures
matching the frozen conventions (does not depend on the real renderer's output).
